sections.heading: How Our Roofing Contractors Perform Spray Foam Roofing

runs.v: Substrate Preparation and Moisture Testing

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing core-samples and moisture-tests the substrate first, because trapped moisture causes blistering and adhesion loss, per the SPFA and NRCA.

runs.v: Proper substrate preparation and inspection are crucial, and a water-soaked roof must come off, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4.
Seamless Foam Application and Drainage Slope

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing sprays foam in controlled passes, slopes it for drainage, and coats it to manufacturer specification.

runs.v: Moisture and temperature limit the installation window: Newark's average January low is near 25.5°F, per NOAA 1991–2020 normals at Newark Liberty (EWR), and SPF needs skilled labor for proper adhesion.
Protective Coating and Recoat Cycle

c.v: SPF requires a UV-protective coating, so Newark Quality Roofing recoats on a 10-to-20-year cycle.

runs.v: A written workmanship warranty backs the labor, separate from the manufacturer material warranty, per Owens Corning warranty guidance.

sections.heading: Is Spray Foaming Your Roof a Good Idea? Where Newark Foam Roofing Is Highly Effective

c.v: Spray foaming a roof is a good idea on flat and low-slope roofs that need insulation, have many penetrations, or pond water.

runs.v: Newark foam roofing is highly effective because one layer creates a seamless, monolithic seal with no seams to leak, fills gaps and cracks, stops drafts, and adheres to concrete, wood, and steel decks.

The benefits start with energy: spray foam creates an airtight barrier that can reduce energy loss by up to 40%, can cut energy bills by up to 50% on a poorly insulated building, and helps improve energy efficiency in extreme weather. Fully adhered foam roofing systems resist wind uplift and severe weather better than many seamed systems, and the rigid foam adds stiffness and some structural strength.

sections.heading: Closed Cell Spray Foam Insulation vs. a Spray Foam Roof System

c.v: Learn the two types of spray foam insulation before hiring.

runs.v: Open and closed cell foam are both used for insulation inside attics, walls, and interior areas, open-cell at roughly R-3.5 to R-4.3 per inch; a roof uses only high-density closed-cell foam, considered the roofing type, sprayed on top of the deck and coated for UV protection and durability.

faqs.q: How long does a spray foam roof last?

runs.v: A foam roof lasts 30 or more years when its coating is maintained, often with little more than a recoat every 10 to 20 years, per the SPFA and SPF manufacturers.

faqs.q: Can spray foam roofing be applied over my existing roof?

runs.v: Yes, over a sound, dry roof with fewer than 2 layers, avoiding a tear-off, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4.

faqs.q: What is the R-value of spray foam roofing?

runs.v: An aged R-6.0 to R-6.5 per inch, per the SPFA; a thicker layer raises the total.

faqs.q: Why does spray foam roofing need a protective coating?

runs.v: The foam degrades in sunlight, so the coating shields it from UV, weather, and foot traffic.

faqs.q: How much does spray foam roofing cost in Essex County, NJ?

runs.v: $4–$8 per square foot installed; Newark Quality Roofing provides a free written estimate.

faqs.q: Does a commercial spray foam roof require a permit in Newark, NJ?

runs.v: Yes, when the work covers more than 25% of the roof area in 12 months, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7.

faqs.q: How does spray foam roofing compare to a single-ply membrane?

runs.v: Foam is one seamless, insulated layer; single-ply sheets join at seams, their most common failure point.

faqs.q: What are the disadvantages of a spray foam roof?

runs.v: Recoats every 10 to 20 years, a narrow weather window, the need for skilled installers, and punctures that must be sealed quickly.

faqs.q: Are spray foam roofers the same as foam insulation contractors?

runs.v: Not always: foam insulation contractors mostly work inside attics and walls for builders and homeowners, while a spray foam roof is roofing work on top of the deck.
